name: API Uptime
blurb:
This section tracks measured uptime for 12 AI API providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Cohere, Groq, Cerebras, Deepgram, ElevenLabs, AssemblyAI, Stability AI, Baseten, Fireworks AI, and Lambda. For each provider it records a healthy or unhealthy status at each check and rolls that up into a healthy percentage over the tracked window, alongside a daily count of how many providers are currently healthy.

The status comes from automated checks against each provider's own reported status, run several times a day since mid-August 2026, not from independent synthetic testing of the live API endpoints. That means it reflects what providers disclose about their own availability, which can lag or understate real user-facing disruptions, and short blips between checks may not register at all. It is a directional reliability signal across providers, not a service-level guarantee.

As of September 5, 2026, all 12 tracked providers show healthy status, matching the pattern for most of the past week. Over the full tracked period, reliability is uneven. Lambda stands out as the clear laggard at 56.3 percent healthy across 142 checks, far below the rest of the field. OpenAI is next weakest at 88.5 percent, with Fireworks AI and Anthropic both around 95.9 percent. Six providers, including Groq, Deepgram, AssemblyAI, and Stability AI, recorded 100 percent healthy checks across the entire window.

reading.body:
API availability across major AI providers ranges from perfect to severely degraded, with six providers recording 100 percent uptime since mid-August 2026 while Lambda has operated at only 64.2 percent.

The data reflects provider self-reported status rather than independent testing, so it understates real user-facing outages that occur between automated checks. It shows directional reliability trends across the field, not service-level guarantees. Measurement began at different dates for most providers, with Lambda starting one day later than the rest, giving unequal observation windows.

Most providers cluster in the high 90s, suggesting that API infrastructure for AI services has reached a baseline of operational stability. OpenAI at 87.7 percent stands as a notable exception among the larger players, indicating either sustained infrastructure strain or less reliable disclosure of status. Lambda's 64.2 percent performance across 173 checks reveals a persistent structural problem distinct from the rest of the cohort.

The recent pattern of all 12 providers reporting healthy status most days since late August indicates that failures are episodic rather than systemic. This matters because AI applications that depend on external APIs require routing and fallback logic to handle these outages. As AI workloads grow more compute-intensive and time-sensitive, even brief disruptions can cascade across downstream services and degrade reliability for end users.
